payload.claim: Ola reportedly receives about 80,000 service complaints per month (Sept 2024).
payload.quote: Insiders familiar with the matter revealed that the Bengaluru-based company receives an average of 80,000 service complaints per month, overwhelming its existing service centers.

payload.claim: Many Ola customers reported 30-45 day waits for repairs (2024).
payload.quote: Many customers reported waiting anywhere from 30 to 45 days for repairs, and several have taken to social media, particularly X (formerly Twitter), to air their grievances.

payload.claim: Ola announced HyperService targeting 1,000 service centres by Dec 2024.
payload.quote: Ola Electric will expand its service network to 1,000 centers nationwide by December 2024 ensuring that customers receive timely assistance regardless of their location.

payload.claim: Bajaj and TVS maintained stable electric scooter sales during Ola's 2024 service troubles.
payload.quote: Meanwhile, competitors like Bajaj Auto Ltd and TVS Motor Company Ltd have maintained stable sales, continuing their upward trend in the electric scooter market.

payload.claim: iQube Power mode reaches an indicated 80kph and holds those speeds.
payload.quote: Eco mode caps the speed to 50kph, which is the typical pace in most cities, while Power mode allows you to hit an indicated 80kph.

payload.claim: Chetak indicated 69kph top speed feels compromised on faster roads.
payload.quote: In comparison, the Chetak’s 69kph indicated top speed feels a little compromised on Mumbai’s wider, quicker roads like the Eastern and Western Express Highways that cut across the city.
Even its top speed, at a Vbox verified 99.8kph, is much higher than the Ather, which tops out at a GPS rated 80kph.

payload.claim: Ather 450X is the least comfortable of the four; cramped for riders over 5ft 10in.
payload.quote: The Ather is the least comfortable of the lot by some margin, with the smallest seat and a high-set floorboard resulting in a cramped riding position, especially for riders taller than 5ft 10in.

payload.claim: Chetak and iQube have excellent ergonomics; iQube best two-up seat.
payload.quote: The rider’s triangle is absolutely spot on, and it is a similar case with the TVS iQube as well.

payload.claim: Ola S1 Pro cuts power the moment you touch the brakes; Chetak does so less.
payload.quote: But what’s more annoying is the way in which the S1 Pro cuts the power the moment you touch the brakes.

payload.claim: Ola Eco mode is borderline dangerous in fast city traffic.
payload.quote: Another issue with the Ola is that the new ‘Eco’ mode restricts the acceleration to a pace that is borderline dangerous when surrounded by fast moving big city traffic, and, makes it impossible to climb steep gradients.

payload.claim: Ather 450X Eco mode remains usable below 10 percent battery.
payload.quote: In the case of the Ather 450X, Eco mode is quite usable even when the battery percentage falls below 10 percent.

payload.claim: Real-world range in Bengaluru traffic runs well below certified IDC figures; 20 km/day is a light load.
payload.quote: Certified IDC figures come from controlled test cycles, and real-world range in Bengaluru traffic runs well below them thanks to low average speeds, frequent stops and short bursts of acceleration to clear junctions.

payload.claim: iQube bigger-battery variants offer decent range for daily use.
payload.quote: The bigger battery pack variants offer decent range for daily use

payload.claim: Autocar noted a few suspension-failure cases on Ola S1 Pro were shared online.
payload.quote: there’s also a sense of nervousness that arises every time you hit a big pothole after those few cases of suspension failure were shared online.
